title: Gold Slides Toward Weekly Loss as Oil-Fueled Inflation Fears Mount Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit

body:
Gold prices fell to a one-week low on Friday, with spot bullion dropping 0.6% to $4,619 per ounce and tracking a 1.9% weekly decline — the steepest in over a month. Rising energy prices, stoked by the collapse of US-Iran peace talks and President Trump's rejection of Tehran's nuclear proposal, have rekindled inflation fears and pushed expectations of prolonged higher interest rates.

The Producer Price Index for April came in hotter than expected at 1.4%, reinforcing the view that the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady well into 2026. Futures markets now price in a 31% chance of a rate hike by March 2027, a sharp reversal from earlier rate-cut optimism. The strengthening dollar has added further pressure on bullion, which pays no interest.

Markets are now focused on a scheduled meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, with trade tensions and tariff policy on the agenda. Analysts at Goldman Sachs expect gold to remain range-bound between $4,400 and $4,800 as geopolitical risks balance out rate headwinds.

For Indian-American investors, the picture is doubly complicated. India this week imposed a 15% import tariff on gold and silver, pushing domestic prices higher even as global benchmarks fall. NRIs sending gold home for weddings or festivals now face steeper landed costs. Meanwhile, the rupee's relative stability against the dollar offers a modest buffer for those tracking gold in INR terms.

The oil-inflation nexus remains the wildcard. Brent crude has held above $104 per barrel amid Strait of Hormuz supply fears, and any escalation could push gold back into safe-haven territory. For now, though, the market is pricing in higher-for-longer rates — and gold is paying the price.
author: Diaspora Desk
